claims.claim: Customer and government concentration is a source-addressed execution risk: Infleqtion disclosed that two customers represented 60% and 12% of 2025 revenue, one customer represented 78% of year-end accounts receivable, and U.S. government customers represented about 60% of 2025 revenue.

This concentration creates sensitivity to government budget/procurement changes and customer timing, but it is not evidence of current deterioration; the lawful falsifier is sustained diversification in revenue/receivables or durable contract conversion across commercial customers.

risks.risk: Revenue and receivable concentration can amplify procurement, budget and customer-timing volatility.

unknowns.unknown: Current 2026 customer-level revenue concentration is not quantified in the reviewed Q2 filing and remains an Alpha underwriting input gap.

falsifiers: Material diversification of customer revenue and receivables would reduce concentration risk.
Repeatable commercial deployments outside government channels would weaken the government-dependence thesis.
recommendedUse: source-addressed risk evidence for Alpha underwriting; no numeric score implied
